concept.title: Pseudo-classes
concept.shortdesc: A pseudo-class starts with : and tests something about an element that its name and attributes do not tell, such as its position among its siblings or its language.

conbody.p: Write a pseudo-class after a selector. The rule applies only to elements that pass the test:
The selector reference lists every pseudo-class that CSSMedia accepts.

section.title: Child and sibling position
section.p: Structural pseudo-classes select elements by their position among the elements that share a parent. Text, comments and processing instructions are not counted.
:first-child, :last-child and :only-child count all sibling elements. The -of-type forms count only siblings with the same element name and namespace.

section.title: Nth-position selectors
section.p: An :nth-* pseudo-class selects elements by their numbered position. Positions start at one. odd and even select alternating elements, and An+B describes a repeating sequence.
The of clause of :nth-child() and :nth-last-child() limits the count to siblings that match a selector. The -last- forms count from the end.
:nth-col() and :nth-last-col() select table cells by the position of their column. Columns are found as described in Combinators.

section.title: Root, empty and scope
section.p: :root selects the root element. :empty selects an element with no child elements and no text other than white space. :scope selects the scoping element, which is the root element unless a rule sets another scope.

section.title: Selector-list and relational pseudo-classes
section.p: These pseudo-classes combine selectors. :is() matches an element that matches at least one selector of its list. :where() does the same but adds no specificity. :not() excludes the elements that match its list. :has() selects an element by the elements related to it.
An invalid selector in a :not() list makes the whole selector invalid. :is() and :where() ignore invalid selectors. :matches() is accepted as another name for :is().

section.title: Language and direction
section.p: :lang() selects elements by language. The language of an element is its nearest xml:lang value, or the value that the -cssmedia-lang property gives. See Document language.

:dir(ltr) and :dir(rtl) select elements by text direction. CSSMedia takes the direction from the first strong character in the element's text, as the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm does. Without one, it uses the direction in which the element's language is written, and left-to-right when there is no language. The direction property does not change the result.

section.title: Links and document location
section.p: An XML element is a link only when you make it one with -cssmedia-link, a CSSMedia extension that sets the destination of an element. The destination can be a place in the same document or an external address. See Links.

:link and :any-link select the elements that have a destination. :local-link selects the links that point into the same document. An optional integer limits the number of path segments that are compared.

section.title: States that do not occur in a PDF
section.p: A PDF has no pointer, keyboard focus, media playback, form controls or browsing history. Pseudo-classes that test those states are valid selectors, but they never match an element. Examples are :hover, :focus, :visited, :target, :playing, :checked and :disabled. The same holds for :state() and :heading, because an XML element has no custom state and no heading role.
:read-only and :defined match every element. The selector reference gives the result for each pseudo-class.
